audit.whatIsWrong: 55.56% is drawn from a 9-game sample, so it carries no signal, yet the packet uses it to call the level chart wrong.
audit.why: MC_REAL_GAMES.mel.aatrox is 9. 55.56% is literally 5 wins in 9 games; the mechanical read should drive the chart, not the number.
audit.corrected: Treat this as an unmeasured matchup and let the kit interactions decide the phases. No edit proposed to the win-rate figure itself.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers flatly contradict: CHAMP_FULL says FAVOURED 4/10 with all seven phases to Mel; MC_CONTENT_EXTRA gives Aatrox stages 3-6.
audit.why: Aatrox has a dash (Umbral Dash, 9s), a 825-range pull (Infernal Chains) and passive healing off every hit; Mel has no dash and one root. A 4/10 favoured read is not defensible.
audit.corrected: The content layer's read is the closer one. diff/diffRating could not be edited without breaking the fixed-length rule (FAVOURED->EVEN is -50%), so the phase why-text was rewritten to state the real mechanic instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr claimed "you reflect what he throws". Aatrox throws almost nothing: only Infernal Chains carries the projectile flag; The Darkin Blade is a melee AoE sweep and his autos are melee.
audit.why: Rebuttal's reflect half has one possible target in his entire kit. Its real value here is the damage-prevention half (Riot: "prevents her from taking damage").
audit.corrected: Reframed W as a damage-immunity window rather than a reflect, and pointed it at the third Darkin Blade swing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (W: prevents her from taking damage)

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions Searing Brilliance's stacking projectiles, which is Mel's whole damage pattern.
audit.why: Each ability cast adds three bonus projectiles to her next attack, capped at nine. Casting E, Q and W before the auto is the maximum-value rotation.
audit.corrected: tradeGood now states the three-casts-then-auto sequence explicitly.

audit.whatIsWrong: World Ender was described only as an all-in signal; the text never says who it actually fears.
audit.why: Riot's text: it fears nearby enemy MINIONS. It applies no crowd control to Mel, so there is no CC to play around — only stats and amplified healing.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now states that it fears minions rather than her, so the chains are the thing that actually locks her down.

audit.whatIsWrong: "your only defensive layer is gone for twenty seconds" understates Rebuttal's cooldown by roughly half.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26 seconds. At the levels where this warning matters it is 38 or 35 seconds, not twenty.
audit.corrected: Corrected to 38 seconds at rank 1 in tradeBad, and the same number was added to phases[1].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown section named World Ender as the only thing to track, but World Ender is not what stops Mel from walking away.
audit.why: Infernal Chains is 20/18/16/14/12 seconds. Without it Aatrox has Umbral Dash (9s) to close but nothing to hold her, and Mel outranges him 950 to 825.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and the All-In Windows report row now key the step-up to Infernal Chains' 20-second downtime.

audit.whatIsWrong: Deathbringer Stance's auto-attack reset was never surfaced as a tell.
audit.why: His burst opens on the reset, so the attack wind-up is the cue to step back, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: Added to the Key Ability Interactions report row.

audit.why: Umbral Dash heals passively off every hit on a champion and World Ender amplifies healing, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: The Itemization row already says "Add anti-heal early into his sustain" — left alone; the reason was added to breakdown.mid and phases[3].why instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three dosFull/dontsFull descriptions were pasted from unrelated templates and did not describe their own titles.
audit.why: dosFull[0] "Fan Q across his last-hit positions" was paired with World Ender text; dosFull[2] "Snare the step-up" with a World Ender line; dontsFull[2] "Let him freeze" with the Rebuttal line.
audit.corrected: Each description rewritten to match its title with a real number.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content repeatedly says Mel pokes "with Radiant Volley from 550 range".
audit.why: Radiant Volley's cast range is 950. 550 is her attack range, not her Q range — the distinction is the whole early lane.
audit.corrected: whys[0] and several full-layer lines now use 950 for Radiant Volley and contrast it with his 825-range chains.

audit.whatIsWrong: Golden Eclipse's global range is never used.
audit.why: R range is 25000 and it strikes every Overwhelm-marked enemy regardless of distance, so stacks banked in lane can be cashed after he leaves it.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now says the ultimate is global and can be cashed after he dives elsewhere.

edits.after: Infernal Chains is his only projectile — W blanks damage here, it does not reflect. Stack, then execute at 6.

edits.after: Stack, snare, and execute — but step up on Infernal Chains' downtime, not his. Every commit asks: are the chains up?

edits.after: Aatrox wins by chaining Infernal Chains into Umbral Dash and the third Darkin Blade swing, healing back all your chip.

edits.after: Burning Rebuttal on chip damage and then standing in World Ender range — your only defensive layer is a 38-second cooldown at rank 1.

notes:
Sample size: MC_REAL_GAMES.mel.aatrox is 9 games, so the 55.56% headline is noise. The packet defect "level chart contradicts data" is chasing a 9-game number — I did not reshape the chart to match it.

Unfixable under the fixed-length rule: CHAMP_FULL says diff FAVOURED / 4/10 with all seven phases marked Mel, while the content layer gives Aatrox stages 3-6. Changing diff (FAVOURED -> EVEN is -50% length) or a phase side (Mel -> Aatrox is +100%) is outside the +/-10% band, so both are left for a human. My phase why-rewrites state the true mechanic under the existing labels.

suspectNames false positive: "Solar Snare's" in spikes[0].text is the correct name with a possessive — no change needed.

Kit-flag false positives I deliberately did NOT write from: Aatrox's Infernal Chains carries a derived "grounding" flag, which comes from the words "smashes the ground" in Riot's text. Infernal Chains slows and drags; it does not ground. Nothing in these proposals asserts grounding.

Left alone for lack of a verifiable source: whether Rebuttal's reflect half actually turns Infernal Chains around, and whether it stops the drag as well as the damage. That is spell-shield-eligibility class and is empty in needsResearch. I only claimed the damage-prevention that is in Riot's own text.
